analyst_view.overall: Leaders Barcelona (33 pts, the league's best attack) host Villarreal (9th, 15 pts) at 14:00 on Sunday, before a Champions League trip on Wednesday. Rodri, Xavi Espart and Bardghji are out (in the numbers), and Christensen is now out too after a new injury the numbers don't know; Koundé, Cubarsí, De Jong and Olmo trained normally and should be in the squad, but Saturday's reports expect most of them on the bench, with Fariñas, Eric García, Gerard Martín and Cancelo in defence. Villarreal under Íñigo Pérez miss Diatta (in the numbers) plus Gerard Moreno, Foyth and Akhomach, which the numbers don't know; all their internationals came back fit and they beat Getafe 2-0 before the break. Alejandro Hernández Hernández referees; the numbers count his short record here (3.0 cards in 2 games).

goals.text: The numbers say 4.3 goals, already high, with Barcelona's scoring run and their absences counted. This morning I expected Koundé and Cubarsí to start; now Christensen is injured and both are tipped for the bench, so Barcelona's back line is younger and thinner than the numbers know, while Villarreal's missing Foyth and Gerard Moreno roughly cancel each other; a mild lean up to about 4.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners and already add Villarreal's high recent corner count (41 in six). Barcelona will dominate the ball with Lamine Yamal and Raphinha, and Villarreal's wide men Moleiro and Buchanan are fit; the defensive changes don't change either side's approach, so I stay at 10.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards and already add Villarreal's busy recent card record (15 in six) and Hernández Hernández, trimmed for his low count in two games. The match has no derby or table edge and Renato Veiga is one booking from a ban, which may make him careful; I keep 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, with both sides' recent shooting already added. Barcelona's front line of Yamal, Fermín, Raphinha and Adeyemi or Gordon is at full strength, but Flick may manage minutes before Wednesday's Champions League trip, with Olmo and De Jong on the bench; these roughly balance, so I stay at 28.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, already raised for Barcelona's recent accuracy (40 on target in six). Villarreal without Gerard Moreno create a little less, while a thinner Barcelona defence may let Mikautadze in a bit more; no clear reason to move it, so 10.6.
